description: Opposition to an application (37 CFR Part 2 Subpart A, TBMP): extension of time to oppose, lapse/allowance, standstill and settlement, institution and answer, optional Section 18 counterclaim, discovery, trial, briefs, final decision, appeal (15 USC 1071), plus a parallel infringement-suit branch. Terminal attrs: rb = fraction of rebrand cost incurred, fx = other applicant USD, sh = 1 if the opposer pays a cost share, sw = opposer win fraction, sfx = opposer other USD; opp_hours/opp_fees on edges are the opposer's own cost. A scenario supplies the utility, opponent_objective and stakes from those attrs (see scenarios/ttab-opposition-applicant-defense.json). All probabilities and hours are teaching estimates.

nodes.label: Application published for opposition
nodes.note: Start of the 30-day opposition period after publication (37 CFR 2.101(c)). A matter scenario sets scenario.start to the node matching its current posture.

nodes.label: First extension (30 days, granted on request)
First extension (90 days, good cause)
Second extension (additional 60 days, good cause)
Day 120: opposition period expires unless the applicant consents to the final 60-day extension
nodes.note: Day 120 from publication. The final 60 days (to day 180) is available only on the applicant's written consent or a showing of extraordinary circumstances; settlement talks, letters of protest, pending amendments and civil litigation are not extraordinary (TBMP 207.03).

nodes.label: Standstill: final 60-day extension by consent
nodes.note: Applicant consents to the final extension in exchange for a standstill (no suit, no opposition, talks). Cost of consent: the potential opposer keeps the option to oppose until day 180.

nodes.label: Choose negotiating posture during standstill
Talks led by rebrand-with-transition and cost share
Talks led by coexistence / consent agreement
No consent: the opposer must oppose by end of day 120 or lose the right to oppose
Standstill expired without a deal: the opposer must oppose by day 180 or lose the right to oppose
Application abandoned before any opposition (37 CFR 2.68; no 2.135 judgment)
nodes.note: Before commencement of an opposition the Board has no jurisdiction; express abandonment (37 CFR 2.68) carries no 2.135 judgment. Any use-based dispute outside the Board remains.

nodes.label: Opposition period closed with no opposition filed
nodes.note: Opposition period closed. The opposer loses the opposition but keeps a petition to cancel within 5 years of registration (15 USC 1064(1)) and any infringement action.

nodes.label: Notice of allowance issued; 6 months to file statement of use (extendable to 24 months)
Registered; opposer's residual options (cancellation within 5 years, infringement suit)
Petition to cancel (2(d)) tried to decision
Notice of opposition filed (commenced)
nodes.note: From here, abandonment without the opposer's written consent = judgment against the applicant (37 CFR 2.135). Opposers can add grounds (e.g. void ab initio for wrong applicant / no bona fide intent) after discovery.

nodes.label: Board institutes; answer due 60 days from institution order (historically 40)
Notice of default for no answer: applicant must show good cause
Answer on file; exits and next stage
Suspended for settlement after institution
Opposer decides whether to consent to abandonment
nodes.note: Consent is the opposer's to give. Refusing yields a judgment against the applicant (issue-preclusion value for a later infringement suit, B&B Hardware v. Hargis, 575 U.S. 138 (2015)), so the opposer will not consent for free.

nodes.label: Suspended for settlement after answer
Discovery conference held (Board attorney on request)
Initial disclosures served (30 days after discovery opens)
Discovery open (180 days)
Discovery closed; ACR/trial/settlement decision
Suspended for settlement during discovery
Suspended for settlement after discovery
ACR: stipulated record, Board decides on summary-judgment-style briefs
nodes.note: Accelerated Case Resolution. Cost saving is an assumption (see edge).

nodes.label: Trial periods: pretrial disclosures, plaintiff 30d, defendant 30d, rebuttal 15d
Trial closed; briefing decision
Suspended for settlement before briefs
Final briefs filed (plaintiff 60d, defendant +30d, reply +15d)
Board final decision
nodes.note: Merits probability is the key judgment input and is matter-specific; the authored 0.60/0.34/0.06 split is a teaching placeholder. With the Section 18 counterclaim pleaded (state flag s18) a scenario probability_fn shifts mass; see ttab-opposition-applicant-defense.

nodes.label: Opposition sustained: appeal choice (63 days, 37 CFR 2.145(d))
Federal Circuit decides
District court decides (de novo on new evidence)
Opposition dismissed: the opposer may appeal
Opposer appeal decided
Registrable with restriction: applicant must move to amend
Judgment final; application returns to prior status, notice of allowance
Opposer decides whether to press its use-based claims after the application is gone
Opposer files federal infringement suit
nodes.note: Fees only in exceptional cases (15 USC 1117(a)); no fee shifting otherwise.
